How the song plays

Want the lasers to follow Spotify by themselves? Open Daddy’s Stu with Start Laser Studio and play a song in the Spotify app.

Auto-sync with the mic

While a show plays, the mic hears where the kicks really land and nudges the show so the lasers hit them. It saves the fix for Spotify, MP3s and the page's own player separately, so the next song starts on time.

Make sure it is matched up

1. Test my speaker

The Mac microphone listens to clicks from your speaker and measures its delay. Do this once each time you connect the speaker.

2. Beat check

While the song plays, all lasers hit once on every beat so you can see if they land on the kick.

3. Tap the beat

Tap 8 beats you hear. The page lines this song up and tells you when it is on time.

Start the song first.

    Delay testing

    Playing through—
    Speaker delay—
    Laser delay—

    The saved delay is used by

      1 · Speaker2 · Laser3 · Saved

      Step 1 of 3: How late is the speaker?

      1. Turn on the speaker you'll use, at normal volume. For the DJ setup, set the Mac's sound output to DDJ-FLX4 first.
      2. Keep the room quiet for about 10 seconds.
      3. Press Play the clicks. The Mac plays 10 clicks and its microphone times how long they take to arrive.

      Step 2 of 3: Line up the laser with the sound

      1. Stand where the crowd will be, where you can see the beams and hear the speaker. The clicks start by themselves.
      2. Not sure what to look for? Press Show me what early and late look like: 4 flashes way late, 4 way early, then your setting.
      3. Flash comes after the click? Press Lasers are late. Comes before it? Press Lasers are early. Every press changes the very next flash.
      4. When the flash and the click happen at the exact same moment, press Save.

      8ms laser delay

      The big buttons move 10 ms and the small ones 2 ms. Drag the slider far one way and you'll clearly see the flash move. Keys: ← early, → late, hold Shift for 2 ms.

      Step 3 of 3: Saved ✓

      From now on every show, the DJ page and the auto modes are on time. Test again only if you switch speakers (Daddy’s Stu notices and reminds you) or use a different laser. Want to double-check with real music? Play a show and hold Space: the lasers flash on every beat.

      Any speaker the Mac can hear: a DJ setup, party speakers

      For music the Mac doesn't play itself (your friend's DDJ-FLX4 into his speakers, a party speaker), the Mac listens with its microphone and fires the lasers on the beat it hears. This lines that up by eye, once per place.

      1. Play music on that system with a clear kick drum, at normal volume.
      2. Put the Mac where the crowd will be, or near the speakers.
      3. Press Start the beat flash: every laser flashes white on each beat. Move the slider until the flashes land right on the kicks, then press Save.

      Bluetooth speaker test

      Bluetooth speakers play 150 to 300 ms late (some more), cut off the start of sounds after silence, and drift a little. This test plays straight through the speaker you pick, keeps it awake, times 3 rounds of clicks with the Mac's microphone and keeps the middle one. Then it plays clicks with the lasers flashing on the result, so you can see them land together.

      1. Connect the speaker to the Mac (Bluetooth settings) and turn it up to normal volume.
      2. Put the Mac a few feet from the speaker and keep the room quiet for 30 seconds.
      3. Pick it and press Test this speaker. Then do step 2 (line up the laser) once.

      5W laser

      Your 5W animation laser follows every show, the DJ page and the auto modes, on the beat. This page tests it, sets its brightness, and teaches Daddy’s Stu its channels and pictures.

      Connection

      1. On the laser's screen: DMX Address 8, Channel 16CH, Mode Set DMX.
      2. Key turned to ON, and the interlock plug in the INTER LOCK socket. Without them it never fires.
      3. The Mac's DMX cable in the laser's DMX INPUT. Click Connect laser at the top (quit QLC+ first).

        The signal test takes 14 seconds: it blinks every DMX channel, then only the 5W's, and tells you what to fix from what the laser did.

        Dark, or only a flat line? Find what turns it on shows the 5W a few test pictures; you answer Real picture or Dark / flat line, and it fixes the 5W's settings.

        Lights now but flickers? Stop the flicker tries values on the channel that was fixed until the picture is steady.

        5W auto show

        The music comes in through the Mac's microphone. The Spotify autopilot on the Auto page uses this same show.

        Check my laser

        Do these once, at your own pace. Each one shows one thing on the laser and waits for your answer.

        1
        Light it up · holds one still picture (white, pattern 1, medium size) until you answer.

        2
        Map my laser · about 3 minutes, do it once. One channel at a time sweeps slowly by itself; click what the laser does. Then Daddy’s Stu knows exactly which channel does what on your laser.

        3
        Colors, one at a time · the laser shows one color and waits. Tell it what you see. 7 colors.

        Colors still wrong, or only one or two work? Find my colors walks the color channel through every value; press the color you see each time it changes.

        4
        Moves, one at a time · bigger and smaller, spinning, left and right, up and down, flipping, other pictures, strobe, off and on. Each one repeats slowly until you answer.

        5
        Pick your beam pictures · open the presets: every built-in picture is one click. Save a row of dots as Beam fan and a ring of dots as Beam star (in haze, each dot is a beam). The auto show uses them.

        6
        Watch the show · the demo plays its own 1-minute track (groove, build-up, drop, breakdown, drop) and runs the auto show on it, so you can see it with no mic.

        Also aim the laser itself so the middle of its range is above head height, and mount it high. If you change Phase on the laser's menu, check which way is up again.

        Brightness

        60%

        More tools · the 30-second test, the sound + laser test, and channel numbers.

        Tests

        Test the laser runs 17 short steps (about 30 s): each color, small and big, spinning, moving, flipping, next pattern, flashing, half brightness, off. Watch that each one does what it says. Sound + laser test plays clicks through your speaker and flashes the 5W on each one.

        Channel numbers (advanced) · which channel does what, and each color's value. Only change these if Claude asks, or with the laser's manual.

        These are a guess from the manual of a laser with the same menu. Press Try it on each row: the laser should do what the row says for 4 seconds. If something else happens, pick another channel. Best: send Claude a photo of the 16CH chart in your manual.

        Group 1, pattern 1

        Play through shows a new picture every 2.5 s. Press a Save button whenever one looks right.

        Set up my laser

        Do this once. It starts from what the Color Waves pad sends (that lights your laser), moves one channel at a time, and you press what changed. Then shows, auto modes and the test all know your laser.

        Each slider is one channel. Explore walks one from 0 to 255 while you watch; type what happened and press Mark. Copy my notes gives Claude everything to set the laser up exactly.

          Simple desk

          Like the Simple Desk in QLC+: one fader for each DMX channel, so you can see the signal and try things by hand. The faders follow what the lasers get. Move one and the desk takes over; press Release (or start Auto, a show or the DJ page) and the music gets the lasers back.

          Faders · one for every channel the lasers use

          Each fader is one DMX channel (0 to 255). Green: the U'King. Blue: the 5W.

          Presets · every built-in picture, one click

          On most lasers like this one: groups 1–2 are simple shapes, group 3 outlined shapes, group 4 dots (each dot is a straight beam in haze, the festival look), group 5 holiday shapes, groups 6–7 moving animations. Yours may differ: the tour shows every one. Until you mark some, the Presets show uses groups 4, 6 and 7 for the drops and 1–2 for breakdowns.

          Your saved pictures

            Helios & ILDA

            The Helios is a small USB box that sends the laser's ILDA input exactly what to draw, point by point. Over DMX the laser can only pick one of its built-in pictures. With the Helios, Daddy’s Stu draws the beams itself: straight beams anywhere, the ring collapse, your own drawings, real brightness, smooth movement, and no guessing the DMX chart. The Helios show on the Auto page uses all of it. Until the Helios arrives, everything here shows in the preview (press Helios show demo).

            Connection

              1. Plug the Helios into the Mac with its USB cable, then press Connect Helios and pick it (only the first time; after that it connects by itself).
              2. Plug a DB25 ILDA cable from the Helios into the laser's ILDA IN (the wide 25-pin socket, not the RJ45 one).
              3. Key on, interlock plug in. If the laser keeps playing its own patterns, look in its menu for an ILDA mode; many lasers switch to ILDA by themselves when the cable is in.
              4. Press a test below. The laser should draw the same thing as the preview. Then press Which way is up: the green arrow should point up with the red beam on the right (if not, tick the flips in Settings). Crowd safe depends on it.

              Test and preview

              Settings

              The Helios is faster than DMX, so it has its own timing. If its beams look late on the kick, move this right; early, move it left.

              The mirrors lag a little behind the colors. Press Color shift check and move this until each dash ends right on a corner.

              Crowd safe works here too: with it on, every look of the Helios show is made for the space above heads, and anything that would land lower is blanked.

              Draw your own

              Hold the click on your trackpad and move to draw a line. Dots makes a beam where you click (in haze, every dot is a straight beam). Save it, then press Play, or pick My drawings (or the Helios show) on the Auto page. Drawings react to the music: kicks punch them bigger, claps flash them white, loud parts make them bigger, build-ups spin them up and drops make them jump in colors.

              Laser shows from other software come as .ild files. Your drawings can be saved as .ild too.

                Setup

                Laser

                Quit QLC+ first, because only one app can use the adapter.

                Spotify Link

                Lets the lasers follow the Spotify app on this Mac (the Spotify autopilot on the Auto page uses it).

                1. Open Daddy’s Stu by double-clicking Start Laser Studio in the Laser Sync folder. It reads Spotify by itself now.
                2. The first time, your Mac asks to let Terminal control Spotify: press OK. (If you said no: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation → Terminal → turn on Spotify.)
                3. Play a song in the Spotify app. The dot at the top turns green: Spotify linked.

                Not running yet.

                DJ board (DDJ-FLX4) and the Yamaha speakers

                1. Plug the DDJ-FLX4 into the Mac with its USB cable. rekordbox plays through it.
                2. Speakers: from the FLX4's MASTER OUT (red and white jacks on the back), left goes to sub A INPUT L and right goes to sub B INPUT R. Then each sub's OUTPUT goes to the HS7 on that side. These are wired speakers, so they add no delay. Skip Bluetooth for laser shows.
                3. In rekordbox, turn on LINK in the top bar, and press BEAT SYNC on both decks.
                4. Double-click Start Link Bridge (in the Laser Sync folder) and leave it open. The first time, it installs what it needs.
                5. Open the DJ page here, pick DJ Link, and press Start DJ lights. Then hold Space and line up the flashes with the kick.

                No LINK button in his rekordbox? Pick Listen with the mic instead.

                Lasers from left to right

                Hold a tile on the Show page to light only that laser.
